page: Microsoft Azure FX16mds_v2 is a compute and memory intensive virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz with 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. The processor features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512, AMX-INT8, and AMX-TILE instruction sets. It includes 336.0 GB of system memory, providing 21.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with a 944 GB local NVMe SSD. It does not include a GPU.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded compute performance enabled by the 4.2 GHz clock speed. In Geekbench testing, the server achieved a single-core score of 2217.0, with upper-percentile outcomes in text processing (2988.0) and image processing (14053.0). Data compression tests showed strong throughput, reaching 34.55 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 14.35 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Small-model LLM text generation reached 429.6 tokens per second. Multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core (17786.09) and Geekbench multi-core (13065.0), placed in the average tier. Uncached memory read bandwidth tested at 82.67 GB/sec, while synthetic memory testing via PassMark scored in the lower quartile.

Qualitatively, the FX16mds_v2 offers high resource efficiency for tasks that require large amounts of memory alongside high single-core processor frequency, avoiding the necessity of provisioning larger core counts merely to acquire sufficient memory capacity. The primary hardware tradeoff is a moderate aggregate multi-core throughput due to the 16 vCPU footprint. The system is suited for in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational databases with large buffer pools, data decompression pipelines, and CPU-based inference workloads.
